verdict.rationale: TruffleHog scans git repositories, filesystems, Docker images and other sources for over 800 secret types, which implies projects can be scanned whatever language they use. There is also a documented Husky hook path for JavaScript/Node.js projects. However, the evidence never states language or package-ecosystem coverage, and nothing shows it understands package manifests, lockfiles or dependency ecosystems. Missing for 10: an explicit language-agnostic or per-language support statement, package-ecosystem (manifest/registry) scanning coverage, and independent corroboration of accuracy across languages.
